cards.text: Solomon, David's son, is the new king of Israel, and he's got his kingdom locked down tight. The LORD his God is with him and lifts him up HIGH. And the first thing the new king does is call a meeting with every commander, every judge and every family leader in all Israel.

cards.question: Solomon takes that whole assembly on a trip to the high place at Gibeon. Why Gibeon?

answers.text: God's Tent of Meeting was there
The ark of God was kept there

cards.text: That's the very tent Moses, the servant of the LORD, made back in the wilderness. Friend, that tent has been through more moving days than anything I own, and I lived in a JUNK DRAWER.

cards.question: The ark of God isn't at Gibeon with the tent. David had brought it from Kiriath-jearim. Where did David put the ark?

answers.text: In a tent he pitched in Jerusalem
In a house he built in Hebron

cards.text: But Gibeon still has the bronze altar that Bezalel son of Uri made, sitting right before the tabernacle of the LORD. So that's where Solomon and the assembly inquire of Him.

cards.question: On the bronze altar at the Tent of Meeting, Solomon offers a ___ burnt offerings before the LORD.

cards.text: A THOUSAND. And I used to think two hundred cookies made a big day. That night, God appears to Solomon.

cards.question: God appears to Solomon that night at Gibeon. What does God tell him?

answers.text: Ask and I will give it to you
Build Me a house in Jerusalem
Rise and go back to your people

cards.text: Solomon answers. He says God showed much loving devotion to his father David and made Solomon king in his place, and he asks God to let His promise to David be fulfilled.

cards.question: Solomon tells God how big the people he's been made king over is. He says they're as numerous as what?

cards.text: Then Solomon asks, "For who is able to govern this great people of Yours?" Friend, I couldn't keep six little cookie cutters from wobbling off ONE counter.

cards.question: God said ask, and Solomon has a whole nation to lead. What does Solomon ask God to grant him?
When God answers, He says Solomon asked for riches and honor along with wisdom.
God grants Solomon the wisdom and knowledge he asked for. What does God say He'll give him on top of that?
God says Solomon's riches and honor will be unlike anything given to the kings ___ him or ___ him.

cards.text: So Solomon leaves Gibeon, goes to Jerusalem and reigns over Israel. God said ASK, and the man picked wisdom, while I'd have asked for a bigger oven and felt GREAT about it.

Then the riches pile up: 1,400 chariots, 12,000 horses, and a horse and chariot trade reaching from Egypt and Kue out to the kings of the Hittites and Aram. The king makes silver and gold as common in Jerusalem as stones, so somebody's kicking a rock on the way to work and it's GOLD.

findings.problem: The joke doesn't click. 'More moving days than anything I own, and I lived in a JUNK DRAWER' has no shared action. Living in a junk drawer is about sitting still and being forgotten, not moving around, so the punchline leaves the baker asking what the drawer has to do with moving.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: Same joke, failing the stranger test. A stranger reading this card would say 'huh?' at the punchline.

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: Bezalel son of Uri appears here for the first time, but the card never says who he is. It doesn't mention that he was the craftsman who made the tabernacle furnishings in the wilderness (Exod 31:2-5).

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences: 'A THOUSAND.' / 'And I used to think two hundred cookies made a big day.' / 'That night, God appears to Solomon.' Only the opening card may have three.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card asks the baker to guess the image in Solomon's comparison: dust of the earth, stars in the sky or sand on the seashore. Nothing earlier lets the baker reason it out. This is the same kind of detail guess as the Psalm 23 oil example.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The joke contradicts the backstory. Papa Dorin says he couldn't keep his six cutters from wobbling off the counter. The backstory says he caught them with his mustache when they wobbled too close to the edge. A joke may make up small moments, but it can't change what the Dorinverse story already says.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: The joke turns the text's simile into a literal claim. In the joke the rock *is* gold, but the text says gold was as common as stones. The joke also mixes the modern 'on the way to work' image into the Bible scene instead of keeping one separate comparison. Together these muddy the fact the card just stated.

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates the stop by a wide margin. Of 9 choice cards, 6 are multiple choice (cards 2, 4, 8, 10, 12, 14), 2 are fill in the blank (cards 6, 15) and 1 is true or false (card 13).

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: Too many choice cards are pure discovery with no context to reason from. These are card 4 (where David put the ark), card 6 (a thousand burnt offerings, a bare number guess), card 8 (God's exact words) and card 10 (dust of the earth). That leaves only about half of the 9 choice cards as informed guesses.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.
